source: www/vpn/faqs and www/directconnect/faqs (snapshots fetched 2026-10-05); parsed indexes corpus/faq/vpn.jsonl and directconnect.jsonl

d12-150.note: The FAQ says 1.25 Gbps per tunnel; the large-bandwidth tunnel (5 Gbps) is in the user guide, and the FAQ itself says 1.25Gbps and 5Gbps for private IP VPN (site-to-site-vpn-faq-private-ip-bandwidth). Writers must not call 1.25 Gbps the only tunnel size. Volatility is frequently-changing so the currency vote runs.

d12-153.note: The VPN FAQ billing answer differs from vpc-faq-vpn-connection-hour-billing (which also states partial hours and data transfer rates); both are kept because they quote different pages.

d12-158.note: The FAQ answer on the SLA is only 'Yes, AWS Direct Connect offers an SLA. Details are here.'; the SLA terms are on www/directconnect/sla (numbers lens).

d12-161.note: The FAQ is silent on a fee for early cancellation beyond 'you may cancel at any time'. Flat-rate billing of dedicated connections (2026-09-15) is not examinable yet; the port-hour answer is the examinable one.

d12-162.note: The FAQ still states 100 routes per BGP session and no mention of prefix controls (up to 1,000, GA 2026-08-20, not examinable yet).

disagreements_for_the_conflict_queue_and.note: FAQ says Client VPN does not support posture assessment; the user guide page describes Client VPN device posture (device trust providers CrowdStrike, Jamf, JumpCloud; re-evaluated every 5 minutes). The guide is the newer source. The numbers/changes lens must date the feature; the writer must not repeat the FAQ answer.
FAQ item 16 gives 1.25 Gbps per tunnel with no mention of 5 Gbps tunnels, while FAQ item 36 mentions 1.25Gbps and 5Gbps for private IP VPN.
FAQ item 119 says 4200000000 to 4294967294 is NOT currently supported for a customer gateway; check cgw-options before the writer uses it.
Compare the six transit gateways per Direct Connect gateway with the quotas page.
Compare 51 virtual interfaces per dedicated connection with the quotas page row.

Item 125 says the Direct Connect gateway does not support VPN CloudHub; item 131 says existing CloudHub keeps working when a VIF is attached to a virtual private gateway directly. Both statements stand; the writer should not say CloudHub cannot work with Direct Connect.

not_added_on_purpose: VPN FAQ item 9 (Site-to-Site VPN connects the VPC to the data center, IPsec, no internet gateway required): covered by the existing canon fact vpc-faq-site-to-site-vpn-ipsec (same text on the VPC FAQ); reuse it.
VPN FAQ item 8 (instances without public IP use NAT gateway or the virtual private gateway): covered by vpc-faq-private-instances-via-vgw.
Pure pointer answers (VPN FAQ item 6 'details can be found in our documentation', Direct Connect FAQ items 109 and 128 'refer to the quotas page'): nothing to quote.
Hosted desktop client operating-system list (VPN FAQ item 83): very volatile and not an exam topic.
